problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2x-y}{x}\,.
$$

feedback.problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
{e}^{2x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2{e}^{x}y-x=0
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2{e}^{x}y-x & =0 \\ {e}^{2x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2{e}^{x}y & =x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{{(2{e}^{-x})}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}y & ={{{e}^{-2x}x}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=2{e}^{-x}$ and $Q(x)={e}^{-2x}x.$
